title: Is Group Gorilla Trekking in Uganda Possible When Your Party Is Bigger Than Eight?
meta_title: Group Gorilla Trekking in Uganda Beyond the 8-Person Limit
meta_description: Group gorilla trekking in Uganda: how the 8-per-family rule works, permit costs, the best Bwindi sector for big parties and how to plan logistics.
excerpt: Group gorilla trekking in Uganda means splitting your party across several gorilla families. Here is how permits, sectors, vehicles and teams work for clubs, schools and families.
content:
Group gorilla trekking in Uganda works for any size of party, but no gorilla family takes more than eight visitors a day. A group of 16 is split across two families and 24 across three, usually in the same Bwindi sector on the same morning. Every trekker needs a permit and must be at least 15.

That eight-person rule shapes every part of group gorilla trekking: which sector you base in, how many vehicles and lodges you need, and how early you book. This guide covers it for club secretaries, school leaders and family organisers. If you want us to handle the planning, our page on how to organise a group safari with Divulge explains how we quote and book for groups.

Quick Facts

  • Team size: Group gorilla trekking teams of up to 8 people per gorilla family, for 1 hour a day
  • Minimum age: 15 for gorilla trekking; 12 for chimpanzee trekking in Kibale
  • Permit price: US$800 per foreign non-resident; US$600 in April, May and November from January 2027 (checked November 2026)
  • Where: Bwindi Impenetrable National Park (four sectors) and Mgahinga Gorilla National Park, southwest Uganda
  • Trek length: Usually 2 to 6 hours on steep, muddy forest trails
  • Getting there: About 8 to 10 hours by road from Entebbe, or a scheduled light-aircraft flight of roughly 1 to 1.5 hours to Kihihi or Kisoro
  • Best months: June to September and December to February are drier; November is wetter and, from 2027, cheaper

How Does Group Gorilla Trekking in Uganda Work?

Group gorilla trekking in Uganda works by booking permits for several habituated gorilla families in one sector on one date. Rangers brief everyone together at the park office, then divide the party into teams of up to eight, one team per family. After the hour with the gorillas, the teams meet again at the lodge.

The Uganda Wildlife Authority sets the rules in its official conservation tariff: a maximum of eight visitors per gorilla group, one hour per group per day, and a minimum age of 15. The limits protect the gorillas from stress and human illness, and are not relaxed for large bookings.

On a group gorilla trekking day your party will not all see the same gorillas. One team may reach a big family on a gentle slope in an hour, while another climbs for four. Explain this before anyone pays, so nobody feels short-changed over dinner.

How many gorilla families does a group need?

For group gorilla trekking, divide the number of trekkers by eight and round up. The harder part is balancing teams, because couples and friends want to stay together, so build teams around those sub-groups first.

Group size (trekkers)Gorilla families neededPlanning note
Up to 81Any sector works; the simplest group gorilla trekking booking
9 to 162Buhoma or Rushaga can usually hold two families on one date
17 to 243Rushaga is the most realistic single-sector choice
25 to 324Often split across two sectors or two trekking days
33 or more5+Stagger the group over consecutive days or combine Bwindi with Mgahinga

Above about 24 people, group gorilla trekking on two consecutive days is often easier: half the party treks while the other half does a community walk, then they swap, and you need half the vehicles at the trailhead.

What Do Gorilla Permits Cost for a Group?

Gorilla permits for group gorilla trekking cost the same per head as for a solo traveller: US$800 per foreign non-resident, with no group discount (checked November 2026). For 16 trekkers, permits alone total US$12,800. Confirm current fees before collecting deposits.

The Uganda Wildlife Authority tariff for January 2027 to June 2028 also lists cheaper permits for April, May and November, a real saving for a large group willing to accept wetter trails.

Permit typeForeign non-residentForeign resident
Gorilla trekking, standard monthsUS$800US$700
Gorilla trekking, April, May, November (from January 2027)US$600US$500
Gorilla habituation (Rushaga, up to 4 people), dates in 2026US$1,500Check with UWA
Gorilla habituation, from January 2027US$1,800US$1,500
Chimpanzee trekking, Kibale (from January 2027)US$250US$200

East African citizens pay UGX 300,000 per gorilla permit, which matters for Nairobi or Kampala clubs and schools. Foreign non-residents must book through a licensed tour operator.

Rescheduling and name changes

The tariff charges 25% of the permit fee for late rescheduling and 50% for moving a permit to another location. In group gorilla trekking someone usually drops out, so collect passport names early and agree who pays if a member cancels. Our travel insurance page explains the cover we suggest.

Where group gorilla trekking saves money

Group savings come from costs that do not scale per head: one driver-guide and vehicle cost much the same for four people or six, and lodges may offer better terms for a block of rooms. On our club itinerary, every seventh place is free for each six paying travellers.

Which Bwindi Sector Suits a Large Group?

Rushaga, in southern Bwindi Impenetrable National Park, suits large groups best because it has the most habituated families, roughly seven to nine. Buhoma in the north has easier walking and is near Kihihi airstrip, so it suits groups of up to about 16 with less confident hikers.

SectorHabituated families (approx.)Best for
Buhoma (north)3 to 5Mixed-fitness groups of up to 16; gentler terrain, near Kihihi airstrip
Ruhija (east)About 4Fit groups; higher ground at around 2,350 m, cooler and steeper
Rushaga (south)7 to 9Groups of 17 to 24 in one sector; also the only habituation base
Nkuringo (south)About 3Small, fit teams; the steepest climbs in Bwindi

Family numbers shift as gorilla groups split and merge, so check availability per date. Avoid splitting one party across Buhoma and Rushaga on the same morning: they are three to four hours apart by road. Buhoma and Ruhija are about an hour apart, so that split is workable for group gorilla trekking when Buhoma alone is full.

Mgahinga Gorilla National Park, near Kisoro, has a single habituated family, a useful overflow for one team of eight when Rushaga is full. For more on the forest, see our Bwindi gorilla trekking guide to sectors and permits.

Moving and Housing a Group Around Bwindi

A group heading to Bwindi needs a vehicle, flight and rooming plan, because the forest is remote and its lodges are small. Plan on about six travellers per safari vehicle so everyone has a window seat, and book rooms as early as permits.

Road or fly-in?

The road from Entebbe to Bwindi takes around 8 to 10 hours, so most group gorilla trekking itineraries break it with stops in Kibale or Queen Elizabeth National Park. Scheduled light aircraft fly from Entebbe to Kihihi (for Buhoma and Ruhija) and Kisoro (for Rushaga and Nkuringo) in roughly 1 to 1.5 hours. They are small single-engine planes, so a big group may need to split across flights or charter.

Rooms and meals

Many Bwindi lodges have only a handful of rooms, so a party of 20 may need two neighbouring properties. Ask members early whether they will share twins or pay single supplements, which move the per-person price more than anything else in a group quote.

How Fit Does Everyone in the Group Need to Be?

Everyone on a group gorilla trekking trip should manage two to six hours on steep, wet forest paths at roughly 1,200 to 2,600 m. Rangers try to send fitter trekkers to families further away, and porters can be hired at the trailhead to carry bags.

Build each team so it moves at a similar pace, and be honest with slower members about what a hard day looks like. Our article on how hard gorilla trekking really is is a useful link to send to members before they commit, alongside our gorilla trekking packing list.

If a few members want longer with the gorillas, the habituation experience in Rushaga takes up to four people for around four hours, while the rest do a standard trek. Our comparison of gorilla trekking vs habituation sets out the trade-off.

Building a Group Itinerary Around the Gorilla Trek

A group gorilla trekking itinerary works best with the trek near the end, after days that get everyone used to early starts and forest walking. Seven to ten days lets you add chimpanzees in Kibale, the Kazinga Channel and, on longer trips, Murchison Falls.

DayWhereGroup highlight
1Entebbe or KampalaArrivals on different flights, welcome briefing
2 to 3Kibale National ParkChimpanzee trekking in small teams and a wetland walk
4Queen Elizabeth National ParkGame drive and Kazinga Channel boat trip
5 to 6Bwindi Impenetrable National ParkGroup gorilla trekking day, then a community walk
7Back to EntebbeDrive, or fly from Kihihi or Kisoro

Chimpanzee trekking in Kibale also runs in small ranger-led parties, so it doubles as a rehearsal for group gorilla trekking. The Kazinga Channel boat trip is the opposite: the whole group sits together.

Is a Private Group Trip Better Than Joining Strangers?

A private group trip usually beats joining strangers on a scheduled departure, because you control the dates, the pace and who shares each vehicle. For group gorilla trekking, that means teams built around friendships and fitness.

A private trip also lets you add what your members care about, such as an evening talk or a celebration dinner. Members can arrive on different flights and pay separately. Our main group safaris page covers the club, school and corporate trips we run.

Insider Tips for Group Organisers

  • Lock the permits first: Confirm gorilla permits for every family before booking lodges or flights; they are the scarcest part of group gorilla trekking
  • Collect passport names early: Permits are issued in each trekker's name, and changes cost money
  • Build teams by pace: Tell us who are the strongest and slowest walkers so rangers can match teams to families
  • Hire porters: Porters earn a fair wage from local communities and make a hard trek far easier
  • Plan a buffer day: Weather and road delays happen; a spare day before the trek protects the most expensive day of the trip
  • Think about the under-15s: Plan a chimpanzee trek, nature walk or community visit for members too young to trek gorillas

Frequently Asked Questions

How many people can go gorilla trekking together in Uganda?

Group gorilla trekking in Uganda is capped at eight visitors per gorilla family per day, for one hour with the gorillas. A larger party is split across two or more families, usually in the same Bwindi sector, so everyone treks on the same morning and meets again for lunch. A group of 20 needs three families.

Do groups get a discount on Uganda gorilla permits?

Groups do not get a discount on Uganda gorilla permits. The Uganda Wildlife Authority charges every foreign non-resident US$800 per trek, with US$600 permits for April, May and November dates in its January 2027 to June 2028 tariff (checked November 2026). Group gorilla trekking savings come from shared vehicles, guides and rooms, not from the permit.

How far ahead should a group book gorilla permits in Uganda?

A group should book Uganda gorilla permits as soon as dates are fixed, ideally six to twelve months ahead for June to September and December to February. Large groups need several families in one sector on one day, which sells out long before a single permit does. Late rescheduling costs 25% of the permit fee.

Can a group with teenagers go gorilla trekking in Uganda?

A group with teenagers can go gorilla trekking in Uganda only if every trekker is 15 or older on the day. Younger members can stay at the lodge, join a community or Batwa walk, or track chimpanzees in Kibale, where the minimum age is 12, so families and school groups can still travel together.

Which Bwindi sector is best for a large group?

Rushaga, in southern Bwindi, is usually the best sector for a large group because it has the most habituated gorilla families, roughly seven to nine. That makes it easier to fit 16 to 24 people into one sector on one morning. Buhoma in the north suits groups of up to about 16 who want gentler trails.

Final Thoughts

Group gorilla trekking in Uganda comes down to one rule, eight people per family, and planning around it: enough permits in one sector, teams matched by pace and a route that builds to the big day. Lock the permits early and the rest falls into place.
